stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Relocates to 5K SF at GFP’s 515 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Zimmet Law Group is relocating its practice inside Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet signed a 5,476-square-foot lease for a newly completed space inside GFP Real Estate’s 515 Madison Avenue, also known as the DuMont Building. Located at the corner of East 53rd Street, the 42-story office tower is just one block south of Zimmet’s current abode in RFR Holding’s 477 Madison Avenue. Zimmet’s practice areas range widely, from matrimonial and family law to real estate matters. The law firm was represented by Savitt Partners’ Elliot Zelinger, while GFP’s Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone negotiated in-house for the landlord. Zelinger did not respond to a request for comment. Asking rent for the nearly 10-year lease term was not disclosed, but office asking rents in Midtown averaged $88.50 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield data. Zimmet is expected to take occupancy at 515 Madison later this year, according to GFP, following the completion of its new space. Zimmet’s office did not respond to a request for comment on the relocation. Earlier this year, GFP took full ownership of the 350,000-square-foot Class A tower after securing an $86.5 million refinancing deal with Apple Bank, which enabled the buyout of ATCO Properties & Management’s remaining 40 percent stake in the property. By late February, the landlord had secured 12,000 square feet of new leasing activity, Commercial Observer reported. GFP announced another 9,000 square feet of deals in late July, including leases for investment firm T7 Capital, aesthetic training provider Innovation Training Specialist and Widowski Law Group. Other tenants at 515 Madison include alternative asset manager Whitebox and therapy provider Manhattan Psychiatry Group. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group leases 5,476 SF at 515 Madison Avenue, Manhattan Midtown.
Midtown office asking rents average $88.50/SF (Q2 2026); Plaza District remains competitive.
Tenant flight from 477 Madison signals consolidation within premium Midtown corridor.
stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group signed a nearly 10-year lease for 5,476 SF of newly completed space at GFP Real Estate's 515 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from 477 Madison Avenue one block north. Average asking rents in Midtown stood at $88.50/SF in Q2 2026. The firm expects occupancy later in 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Signals stable office leasing in Midtown Manhattan, but office demand does not translate to residential demand or supply pressures in the metro.

stories.title: Sixth Street Acquires Iconic Pier House Hotel in Key West for $190M
stories.excerpt: An iconic luxury hotel in Key West, Fla., is changing hands. Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital have acquired Pier House, a longstanding 142-room oceanfront resort in downtown Key West, from Braemar Hotels & Resorts in a $190 million deal, according to a release from Sixth Street. Starwood Property Trust provided the debt financing, the amount of which has not been disclosed, while the Plasencia Group advised Braemar Hotels & Resorts on the sale. Aman Gupta, principal at Sixth Street, noted in a statement that Pier House has access to a private beach and includes unobstructed sunset views for its guests while also being in the heart of Downtown Key West. “This investment reflects Sixth Street’s commitment to identifying high-quality hospitality assets where we can drive long-term value,” said Gupta. Located at 1 Duval Street, Pier Street sits on five acres of beachfront land along the famous Duval Street, a top tourist destination and walkable retail and entertainment thoroughfare. The resort first opened in 1967 and had been owned by Braemar Hotels & Resorts since 2014. On-site amenities include two oceanfront restaurants, a spa, a fitness center, an oceanfront pool and 3,000 square feet of event space. “We believe Pier House represents an opportunity to acquire a historic luxury resort in one of the country’s most supply-constrained and sought-after tropical leisure markets,” said Gupta. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Sixth Street Partners + Riller Capital acquire Pier House Resort, Key West, $190M.
142-room oceanfront luxury asset on 5 acres; Starwood Property Trust financed debt.
Beachfront location at 1 Duval Street; private beach access and high-end positioning.
stories.summary: Sixth Street Partners and Riller Capital acquired Pier House Resort & Spa, a 142-room luxury oceanfront resort in Key West, for $190 million from Braemar Hotels & Resorts. The asset sits on five acres at 1 Duval Street with direct waterfront access, two dining venues, spa, pool, and 3,000 SF of meeting space. Starwood Property Trust provided debt financing.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development. Hospitality asset acquisition by institutional capital; no supply, demand, or cost signals for apartment communities.

stories.title: Heights Advisors Files Plans to Build 606 Affordable Units in the Bronx
stories.excerpt: Heights Advisors, a Brooklyn-based development and investment firm led by founder and president Rachel Foster, is planning to bring 606 affordable housing units to the Bronx’s Soundview neighborhood. The firm filed a land use application Wednesday with the New York City Department of City Planning requesting a zoning amendment and a special permit to build a 21-story mixed-use building with 606 units at 945 White Plains Road. The filing initiates a Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), which typically takes about seven months of public review of the proposed zoning changes, and includes formal hearings before a final vote by the City Council and City Planning Commission. If approved, Heights Advisors’ proposed project would span 515,063 square feet and include 503,095 square feet of residential space and 11,968 square feet of commercial space, the application notes. The Brooklyn developer is seeking construction financing under the New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development’s New Construction Finance Program, which provides funding for the construction of 100 percent affordable multifamily rental projects, according to the filing. Of Heights Advisors’ 606 planned units, approximately 152 are set to be affordable. It’s unclear whether Heights Advisors, which is the ground lessee of 945 White Plains Road on a 99-year ground lease, plans to demolish the current retail property on the site, which is home to a Modell’s Sporting Goods and GameStop. Heights Advisors did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. Other residential developments planned for the Bronx include a 228-unit affordable senior housing development at 3728 Park Avenue, as well as a pair of 99-unit residential buildings at 761-769 East Tremont Avenue. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Heights Advisors files ULURP for 606 affordable units, Soundview, Bronx, 945 White Plains Road.
21-story mixed-use: 503,095 SF residential, 11,968 SF commercial; 515,063 SF total.
Seeking HPD New Construction Finance Program funding; ~7-month ULURP review ahead.
stories.summary: Heights Advisors filed a land-use application for a 21-story mixed-use building with 606 affordable units in the Bronx's Soundview neighborhood at 945 White Plains Road. The project spans 515,063 SF (503,095 SF residential, 11,968 SF commercial) and requires a zoning amendment and special permit through ULURP. The developer is seeking construction financing via HPD's New Construction Finance Program.
stories.impact: Signals strong institutional/nonprofit appetite for affordable multifamily in Bronx submarkets; Heights Advisors' scale and financing pathway indicate viable development economics even in outer-borough affordable. Increased supply in Soundview may moderate future rent growth but strengthens population retention and workforce housing in the borough, supporting long-term demand for additional market-rate infill.

stories.title: City of Mesa Advancing Marriott Hotel Plans
stories.excerpt: The City of Mesa authorized the town’s city manager to negotiate a deal with a developer to construct a 5-story AC Hotel by Marriott on the northeast corner of Main Street and Centennial Way. The 85,000-square-foot hotel would consist of 150 rooms, an outdoor pool and a lounge open to guests and the public. The project is slated to cost $39 million. The terms of the deal would require the city to reimburse up to $288,000 in construction sales taxes generated by the project. The developer would be obligated to license up to 100 parking spaces within a parking garage, which is projected to generate $5 million in revenue over the 50-year term of the parking license. Under state law, the hotel project would be exempt from approximately $2.1 million in property taxes. The post City of Mesa Advancing Marriott Hotel Plans appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: City of Mesa authorized AC Hotel by Marriott, Main & Centennial, 150 rooms, $39M.
5-story, 85,000 SF hotel; city reimburses up to $288K in sales tax; 50-year parking license.
Hotel exempt ~$2.1M in property tax under Arizona law.
stories.summary: The City of Mesa authorized its city manager to negotiate development of a 150-room AC Hotel by Marriott on the northeast corner of Main Street and Centennial Way. The $39 million, 85,000 SF, 5-story project includes an outdoor pool and public lounge. The city will reimburse up to $288,000 in construction sales tax; the developer will license up to 100 parking spaces, projected to generate $5 million over 50 years.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. Hotel development signals downtown Mesa activation and foot traffic, which can indirectly support future mixed-use or residential infill, but no explicit apartment supply, demand, or cost signals present.

stories.title: Madewell To Open New Store at Tishman Speyer’s 1 Rockefeller Plaza
stories.excerpt: Famed denim and clothing brand Madewell is opening a new store at Tishman Speyer’s 1 Rockefeller Plaza, the landlord announced Thursday. The retailer signed a 7,340-square-foot lease at the Midtown landmark, where its new space will open in 2027. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed, but the average asking rent for retail space in Midtown Plaza District was $2,540 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. “Rockefeller Center continues to attract brands that shape culture and consumer behavior globally,” EB Kelly, senior managing director at Tishman Speyer and head of Rockefeller Center, said in a statement. “Madewell’s decision to establish a presence here reinforces the center’s unique ability to combine iconic New York identity with modern cultural relevance.” Newmark brokered the deal for Madewell, while Tishman Speyer was repped in-house by Lucy Phillips. Newmark did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Madewell’s new store at Rockefeller Center will be its eighth location in New York City. “We’re excited to be part of Rockefeller Center, one of New York’s most iconic retail destinations,” Garrett Putney, senior vice president of retail at Madewell, said in a statement. “This store represents an important milestone for Madewell, giving us the opportunity to bring our full brand experience to life in a space that reflects our commitment to quality, style and community.” Built in 1937, 1 Rockefeller Plaza is a 34-story office, dining and shopping center located between West 48th and West 49th streets in Midtown. Office tenants in the building include real estate investment trust Chimera Investment Corporation and investment firm Ulysses Management, while clothing shop Alex Mill has a ground-floor location there. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Madewell signs 7,340 SF lease at Tishman Speyer's 1 Rockefeller Plaza, Midtown.
Retail asking rents in Midtown Plaza District average $2,540/SF (Q2 2026); lease opens 2027.
Tishman Speyer landing marquee retail; no residential component disclosed.
stories.summary: Madewell signed a 7,340 SF lease at Tishman Speyer's 1 Rockefeller Plaza in Midtown Manhattan, with opening planned for 2027. Retail asking rents in the Midtown Plaza District averaged $2,540/SF in Q2 2026. The landlord and retailer emphasized the property's cultural draw and global consumer relevance.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development. Retail leasing in Rockefeller Center reflects strong flagship retail demand in Midtown but does not signal residential supply, demand, or capital dynamics.

stories.title: Porter Kyle Adds New 100-Unit BTR Community to East Valley Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Porter Kyle, a Scottsdale-based Build-to-Rent (BTR) developer and general contractor, opened the doors to The Wayne, a 100-unit BTR townhome community in Chandler, Ariz. Residents are moving in, and the clubhouse and first four buildings at the community have been transitioned to Mark-Taylor for ongoing lease-up and property management. The opening caps a 20-month build by Porter Kyle Builders of a community that was delivered on schedule and under budget. Porter Kyle’s Taylor Shultz added, “This community was built to compete with for-sale product on quality while offering the flexibility of a lease, and the early absorption numbers tell us that resonated with renters from day one.” The Wayne offers one-, two- and three-bedroom townhomes with direct-access two-car garages, and private backyards. Community amenities include a resident clubhouse with coworking spaces and private offices, a fitness center, pool and outdoor kitchen, a dog park, and a community trail system. Porter Kyle has four BTR projects in Phoenix’s East Valley. The post Porter Kyle Adds New 100-Unit BTR Community to East Valley Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Porter Kyle delivered The Wayne, 100-unit BTR townhome community, Chandler, Arizona.
20-month build completed on schedule and under budget; early absorption strong.
Units include 1–3 bedrooms, direct-access garages, backyards; Mark-Taylor managing lease-up.
stories.summary: Porter Kyle completed The Wayne, a 100-unit build-to-rent (BTR) townhome community in Chandler, Arizona, on schedule and under budget in 20 months. Amenities include a clubhouse with coworking, fitness center, pool, dog park, and community trails. Units offer one-, two-, and three-bedroom floor plans with direct-access two-car garages and private backyards. Mark-Taylor is now managing lease-up; early absorption has exceeded expectations.
stories.impact: BTR absorption strength in Chandler signals robust demand for single-family rental product in East Valley Phoenix submarket. On-time, under-budget delivery indicates favorable construction conditions and labor availability in Arizona. Continued BTR supply and competitive absorption versus for-sale may temper future rent growth but confirms sustained demand for flexibility-focused housing; validates continued BTR pipeline in metro.

stories.title: KKR Names Sam Caven, Marshall Nevins New Co-Heads of Acquisitions
stories.excerpt: KKR has appointed Sam Caven and Marshall Nevins co-heads of acquisitions for the Americas, Commercial Observer can first report. Nevins joins KKR from Blackstone, where he was a managing director, leading investments across multiple real estate strategies. Caven has led investment activity across KKR’s U.S. real estate funds since 2024 and previously spent 13 years at Starwood Capital. The new co-heads now join Brett Kelly and Michael Osborne, co-heads of KKR’s real estate equity asset management business, with all four reporting up to Justin Pattner, head of equity for the Americas. “We pride ourselves on continuing to evolve, and sometimes the more profound changes around businesses present themselves as people-related changes,” Pattner said. “We’ve been investing, harvesting, and trying to figure out what our organizational structure should look like on a go-forward basis so that we can maintain performance and grow well into the future, and this was a great time to make those changes.” Nevins’ first day was August 12, and so those changes are now up and running. “As a firm, we’re big believers in if you can find the right co-head model — because people have different perspectives and different strengths — and as long as you have the right organizational structure and the right incentive model, you can be in a situation where one-plus-one is greater than two,” Pattner said. “So, it’s a case of the right time, right people, and we’re pretty excited.” San Francisco-based Caven brings 19 years of experience to his new role. At Starwood, he led acquisitions and dispositions of office, industrial and residential assets and also worked on the formation of Starwood Waypoint Homes and Starwood Real Estate Income Trust. bullets: KKR appoints Sam Caven and Marshall Nevins co-heads of Americas acquisitions.
Nevins from Blackstone (MD); Caven led KKR's U.S. real estate funds since 2024.

stories.summary: KKR named Sam Caven and Marshall Nevins as co-heads of acquisitions for the Americas, effective August 12. Nevins joined from Blackstone, where he was a managing director investing across multiple real estate strategies. Caven has led KKR's U.S. real estate fund investment activity since 2024 and spent 13 years at Starwood Capital. Both report to Justin Pattner, head of equity for the Americas.
stories.impact: Organizational change at a mega-cap real estate investor; no immediate signal on capital deployment, asset-class focus, or rate/cap-rate assumptions. Monitor for future announcements on multifamily acquisition targets or fund closes to assess appetite and pricing discipline in the market.

stories.title: ParkProperty Acquires 280-Unit Buckhead Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: ParkProperty Capital acquired The Jane, a 280-unit multifamily in the Brookwood district of Atlanta, adjacent to Buckhead. The property was traded for $75 million. CWS Capital Partners was the seller. The property was named after the local golf legend Bobby Jones’ putter, Calamity Jane. Brookwood sits adjacent to the Bobby Jones Golf Course. Once called Marquis at Buckhead, The Jane is located steps away from the Beltline Northside Trail along Colonial Homes Drive Northwest. The community features one- and two-bedroom floor plans. Amenities include a saltwater pool, two sundecks, outdoor sporting and recreation area, and a regulation-size Bocce Ball court . ParkProperty Capital plans to renovate the community’s interiors to better align with the property’s branding and pay tribute to its contemporary Southern exterior architecture. ParkProperty Capital purchased an adjacent multifamily property, The Monroe, in 2022. The company owns additional multifamily assets in U.S. metros such as Houston, Charlotte, Austin, Seattle and Phoenix. The post ParkProperty Acquires 280-Unit Buckhead Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ParkProperty Capital acquires The Jane, 280-unit multifamily, Brookwood/Buckhead, Atlanta, $75M.
Asset formerly Marquis at Buckhead; CWS Capital Partners seller; adjacent to Bobby Jones Golf Course.
ParkProperty owns multifamily in Houston, Charlotte, Austin, Seattle, Phoenix; renovation planned.
stories.summary: ParkProperty Capital acquired The Jane, a 280-unit multifamily property in Atlanta's Brookwood district (adjacent to Buckhead), for $75 million from CWS Capital Partners. The property (formerly Marquis at Buckhead) features one- and two-bedroom floor plans and sits steps from the Beltline Northside Trail. ParkProperty plans interior renovations and already owns The Monroe nearby; it also holds multifamily assets in Houston, Charlotte, Austin, Seattle, and Phoenix.
stories.impact: Confirms strong institutional acquisition appetite for stabilized multifamily in Atlanta's Buckhead-adjacent submarkets despite regional supply growth. $75M / 280 units = ~$268K per unit, suggesting moderate cap rates and continued buyer confidence in Atlanta rental demand. ParkProperty's geographic diversification signals operators rotating capital across Sunbelt markets with balanced supply-demand profiles.

stories.title: Sixth Street Pays $190M for Key West Resort
stories.excerpt: Sixth Street acquired the Pier House Resort & Spa, a 142-room, luxury oceanfront resort in Key West, Florida, for $190 million from Braemar Hotels & Resorts. Sixth Street completed the transaction in partnership with Riller Capital. Financing for the transaction was provided by Starwood Property Trust. Situated on five acres at 1 Duval Street, Pier House is located on the waterfront at the gateway to Key West’s Duval Street. Amenities include two oceanfront dining venues, a full-service spa, fitness center, oceanfront pool, 75 linear feet of private beach frontage, and approximately 3,000 square feet of meeting and event space. Sixth Street Real Estate invests directly in properties, provides solutions across the capital structure—including equity, preferred equity, and debt—and partners with sector-related operating businesses. The firm’s real estate investments span a wide range of asset classes, including residential, office, hospitality, industrial, data centers, retail, and other specialized sectors. bullets: Sixth Street Partners + Riller Capital acquire Pier House Resort, Key West, $190M (duplicate of Article 2).

stories.summary: Sixth Street and Riller Capital acquired the Pier House Resort & Spa, a 142-room luxury oceanfront resort in Key West, for $190 million. The property sits on five acres at 1 Duval Street with two dining venues, spa, fitness center, oceanfront pool, 75 linear feet of private beach, and 3,000 SF of meeting space. Starwood Property Trust financed the debt.

stories.title: Xebec Snags Financing for 687K-SF Savannah-Area Industrial Development
stories.excerpt: Xebec closed on $30.49 million in joint-venture equity alongside $39.95 million in construction financing for Black Creek Commerce Center, a three-building Class A industrial development in Black Creek, Georgia. not far from Savannah. JLL secured the construction loan from Seacoast Bank and placed the joint-venture equity with a private investment group. Scheduled to deliver in the third quarter of 2027, the 687,890-square-foot development will feature three buildings spanning 219,170, 284,580 and 184,140 square feet. The development has direct access to U.S. Highway 80, providing immediate connectivity to Interstate 16 and the broader Atlanta market. The Xebec holds a right of first refusal on Phase II, an adjacent 77-acre parcel, through April 2027. The JLL Capital Markets team representing the developer was led by Bobby Norwood and Mark Sixour, along with Britton Burdette, Jim Freeman, Kelsey Bawcombe and Austin Smith. The post Xebec Snags Financing for 687K-SF Savannah-Area Industrial Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Xebec closes $30.49M equity + $39.95M construction loan for Black Creek Commerce Center, Georgia.
687,890 SF Class A industrial (3 buildings); delivery Q3 2027; near Savannah and I-16.

stories.summary: Xebec closed $30.49 million in joint-venture equity and $39.95 million in construction financing for Black Creek Commerce Center, a 687,890 SF Class A industrial development in Black Creek, Georgia (near Savannah). The three-building project (219,170, 284,580, and 184,140 SF buildings) is scheduled for Q3 2027 delivery and has direct access to U.S. Highway 80 and I-16. Xebec holds a right of first refusal on an adjacent 77-acre Phase II parcel through April 2027.
stories.impact: No direct relevance to multifamily development. Industrial capital flowing into Savannah-area logistics; signals regional infrastructure maturity and investor confidence in Southeastern logistics nodes but does not affect residential supply, demand, or financing dynamics.
